title: 7-Day Vietnam Itinerary (March): Hanoi · Ha Long Bay · Hoi An · Ho Chi Minh City
description: Spring in Vietnam — perfect weather for pho in Hanoi's Old Quarter, a cruise through Ha Long Bay's emerald karsts, lantern-lit nights in Hoi An, and street food adventures in Saigon. This classic north-to-south route hits the highlights without rushing.

days.neighborhoods: Old Quarter · Hoan Kiem Lake · French Quarter
days.title: Arrive in Hanoi — Old Quarter Immersion

activities.name: Arrive & Settle In
activities.description: Land at Noi Bai Airport and grab a Grab to the Old Quarter (~45 min, $8-12). Check into your hotel and freshen up. The Old Quarter is walkable chaos — narrow streets, honking motos, and the best energy in Vietnam. Stroll around Hoan Kiem Lake at golden hour. Visit Ngoc Son Temple on the little island (30,000 VND entry). The lake is Hanoi's spiritual heart — locals exercise, play badminton, and socialize here every evening.
details: 💡 Pre-book airport Grab or use the official airport taxi desk to avoid scams
💡 Stay in the Old Quarter (Hoàn Kiếm district) — walkable to everything
📍 Ngoc Son Temple — iconic red bridge, peaceful pagoda on the lake

activities.name: Old Quarter Street Food Crawl
activities.description: Hanoi's Old Quarter comes alive at night. Start at Bia Hoi Corner (junction of Ta Hien and Luong Ngoc Quyen) for 5,000 VND fresh draft beer, then wander the food stalls. Try bun cha, banh cuon, and pho bo from street vendors.

days.neighborhoods: Ba Dinh · West Lake · Old Quarter Markets
days.title: Hanoi Deep Dive — Temples, Markets & History

activities.name: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum & Temple of Literature
activities.description: Start early at the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum (free entry, closed Mon/Fri, opens 7:30 AM). The embalmed body of Vietnam's founding father lies in a granite structure modeled on Lenin's tomb. Then walk to the Temple of Literature — Vietnam's first university, founded in 1070, with serene courtyards and turtle stele.
details: 💡 Mausoleum has strict dress code: no shorts, tank tops, or hats inside
📍 Temple of Literature entry: 30,000 VND (~$1.20)

activities.name: Train Street & West Lake
activities.description: Visit Hanoi's famous Train Street where a railway runs through a narrow residential alley (trains pass ~3:30 PM and 7:30 PM — check schedules). Then head to West Lake (Hồ Tây) for a peaceful walk or cycle. Visit Tran Quoc Pagoda, Hanoi's oldest Buddhist temple on the lake's edge.
details: ⚠️ Train Street cafes have been shut down and reopened multiple times — check current status
📍 Tran Quoc Pagoda — stunning lakeside setting, free entry
tips: Download the 'Grab' app before arriving — it's Southeast Asia's Uber and works for motorbike taxis too. Way cheaper and safer than negotiating with street taxis.

activities.name: Water Puppet Show & Night Market
activities.description: Catch a traditional Vietnamese water puppet show at Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre (shows at 5 PM, 6:30 PM, 8 PM — book ahead). The 50-minute show tells Vietnamese folk tales with wooden puppets dancing on water. Afterward, hit the Old Quarter Night Market (Friday–Sunday evenings).
details: 📍 Thang Long Theatre: 100,000 VND (~$4) — worth every dong

days.neighborhoods: Ha Long Bay · Bai Tu Long Bay
days.title: Ha Long Bay Overnight Cruise

activities.name: Transfer to Ha Long Bay
activities.description: Your cruise operator picks you up from your Hanoi hotel around 8 AM. The drive to Ha Long Bay takes about 2.5 hours via highway. Most reputable cruises include round-trip transport, all meals, kayaking, and cave visits.
details: 💡 Book a 2D/1N cruise on Bai Tu Long Bay for fewer crowds — same limestone karsts, half the tourists
💡 Budget: $80-150/person for a good mid-range overnight cruise. Avoid anything under $60.

activities.name: Board Cruise & Explore
activities.description: Board your junk boat and set sail through thousands of limestone karsts rising from emerald water. After lunch on the boat, kayak through hidden lagoons and swim in the bay. Visit Sung Sot (Surprise) Cave or Titop Island depending on your cruise route.
details: 📍 Ha Long Bay — UNESCO World Heritage Site with 1,600+ limestone islands
💡 March weather is ideal — less rain, less haze than summer, comfortable 20-24°C

activities.name: Sunset, Squid Fishing & Stars
activities.description: Watch the sunset paint the karsts gold from the top deck. Evening activities typically include squid fishing (surprisingly fun), cooking class, or just drinking on deck. Ha Long Bay at night, with stars above and bioluminescent plankton below, is genuinely unforgettable.
tips: Bring motion sickness tablets if you're prone — the bay is calm but the overnight anchor can sway. Also bring a light jacket for the evening deck.

days.neighborhoods: Ha Long Bay · Da Nang · Hoi An Ancient Town
days.title: Ha Long Bay Morning → Fly to Da Nang → Hoi An

activities.name: Sunrise Tai Chi & Disembark
activities.description: Wake early for tai chi on the top deck as mist rises off the bay. After breakfast, the cruise visits one more site (usually a floating village or pearl farm) before docking around 11 AM. Transfer back to Hanoi takes ~2.5 hours.
details: 💡 Book an afternoon flight Hanoi → Da Nang (1.5 hours, ~$40-60 on VietJet)

activities.name: Fly Hanoi → Da Nang & Transfer to Hoi An
activities.description: Catch your afternoon flight to Da Nang (1.5 hours). From Da Nang airport, it's a 30-minute Grab ride to Hoi An (~$8). Check into your hotel — Hoi An has gorgeous boutique homestays for $20-40/night. The Ancient Town is compact and best explored on foot or by bicycle.
details: 💡 Stay near the Ancient Town but not inside the pedestrian zone — quieter and cheaper
📍 An Bang Beach is 4km from town — great for a morning swim

activities.name: Hoi An Ancient Town at Night
activities.description: Hoi An's Ancient Town is UNESCO-listed and absolutely magical at night. Hundreds of silk lanterns illuminate the narrow streets. Cross the Japanese Covered Bridge (Chua Cau), release a floating lantern on the Thu Bon River, and browse the night market. March is perfect — warm, dry, not too crowded.
details: 📍 Ancient Town ticket: 120,000 VND (~$5) — grants entry to 5 heritage sites
💡 The lantern-lit streets are best after 7 PM when the pedestrian zone closes to traffic

days.neighborhoods: Hoi An Ancient Town · An Bang Beach · Tra Que Village
days.title: Hoi An — Tailors, Cooking Class & Beach

activities.name: Cooking Class at Tra Que Herb Village
activities.description: Start with a half-day cooking class (~$25-35) at Tra Que Vegetable Village, 3km from town. You'll bike through rice paddies, pick herbs from the garden, then learn to make banh xeo (sizzling crepes), fresh spring rolls, and cao lau. It's hands-on, fun, and you eat everything you make.
details: 💡 Book Red Bridge or Tra Que classes — both excellent, include market visit
📍 Tra Que Herb Village — an organic farming village that's supplied Hoi An for centuries

activities.name: Tailor Fitting & An Bang Beach
activities.description: Hoi An is the tailoring capital of the world. Get measured for a custom suit, dress, or coat — 24-hour turnaround is standard ($50-200 depending on fabric/item). Then head to An Bang Beach for the afternoon. Lounge chairs, cold beers, and warm water. March seas are calm and perfect for swimming.
details: 💡 Top tailors: Yaly Couture, BeBe, A Dong Silk. Get measured Day 1 for pickup on Day 2
💡 An Bang Beach: rent a lounger ($2-3), order from beachfront restaurants

activities.name: Riverside Dinner & Night Market
activities.description: Have dinner along the Thu Bon River, then browse the Hoi An Night Market for souvenirs, silk lanterns, and street food. Try com ga (chicken rice) from the market stalls — Hoi An's version is uniquely flavored with turmeric.

days.title: Fly to Ho Chi Minh City — Saigon Hustle

activities.name: Morning in Hoi An & Fly to HCMC
activities.description: Pick up your tailored clothes (if ready), grab one last banh mi, and Grab to Da Nang airport for your flight to Ho Chi Minh City (1 hour, ~$30-50). From Tan Son Nhat airport, Grab to District 1 takes 30-45 min depending on traffic.
details: 💡 HCMC traffic is legendary — allow extra time for airport transfers
💡 Stay in District 1 (Ben Nghe/Da Kao area) for walkable access to everything

activities.name: War Remnants Museum & Notre-Dame Cathedral
activities.description: The War Remnants Museum is intense but essential — three floors documenting the Vietnam War from the Vietnamese perspective, with photography exhibits that will stay with you. Afterward, walk to nearby Notre-Dame Cathedral (under renovation but the exterior is beautiful) and the historic Central Post Office designed by Gustave Eiffel.
details: 📍 War Remnants Museum: 40,000 VND (~$1.60) — allow 2 hours
📍 Central Post Office — still functioning, gorgeous colonial architecture inside
tips: Ho Chi Minh City is LOUD. The motorbike traffic is relentless. To cross the street: walk slowly and steadily. Don't stop, don't run — the motos will flow around you. Trust the process.

activities.name: Ben Thanh Market & Bui Vien Walking Street
activities.description: Browse Ben Thanh Market (best before 6 PM for dry goods; the night market outside has great street food). Then head to Bui Vien Walking Street — Saigon's backpacker party street. It's chaotic, loud, and fun. Even if you don't party, walking through is an experience.
details: 📍 Ben Thanh Market — bargain hard, start at 30-40% of asking price
💡 The night food stalls around Ben Thanh are better than inside the market

days.neighborhoods: Cu Chi · District 1 · Tan Son Nhat Airport
days.title: Cu Chi Tunnels & Departure

activities.name: Cu Chi Tunnels Half-Day Trip
activities.description: Book an early morning tour to the Cu Chi Tunnels (70km northwest of HCMC, ~1.5 hours by bus). This underground network of 250km of tunnels was used by Viet Cong soldiers during the war. You can crawl through widened tunnel sections, see booby trap displays, and understand the ingenuity of guerrilla warfare. Go to Ben Duoc site (less crowded than Ben Dinh).
details: 📍 Cu Chi Tunnels: 110,000 VND (~$4.50) entry
💡 Book a small-group tour ($15-25) rather than the big bus tours for a better experience
💡 Go to Ben Duoc section — more authentic and less crowded than Ben Dinh
tips: The tunnels are claustrophobic — if you're not comfortable in tight spaces, you can skip the crawling portion and still see everything above ground.

activities.name: Last-Minute Shopping & Departure
activities.description: Head back to District 1 for last-minute shopping or a final ca phe sua da. If you have time, visit the Jade Emperor Pagoda — one of the most atmospheric temples in the city. Then Grab to Tan Son Nhat airport for your departure.
details: 📍 Jade Emperor Pagoda — stunning Taoist-Buddhist temple, free entry
💡 Allow 1.5-2 hours for airport transfer due to HCMC traffic
